Content

SYMMETRY

  • Symmetry refers to the division of an animal's body into equal, mirror-image halves along a plane (called a plane of symmetry).

Three Types of Symmetry

#### 1. Asymmetrical

  • Lack of symmetry — no plane divides the body into equal halves.
  • E.g. Porifera (sponges).

#### 2. Radial Symmetry

  • Any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides it into two equal halves.
  • E.g. Coelenterata / Cnidaria (jellyfish, hydra), Echinodermata (starfish, sea urchin).

#### 3. Bilateral Symmetry

  • A single plane (the sagittal plane) divides the body into left and right halves.
  • E.g. Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes/Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Chordata (most higher animals).

Quick Reference

SymmetryPhyla
AsymmetricalPorifera
RadialCoelenterata, Echinodermata, Ctenophora
BilateralPlatyhelminthes → Chordata
